memory_candidates.content: Authoring a `## Lean Challenge Statements` block that needs helper DEFINITIONS in scope: declare them as `abbrev`, not `def`. lean-challenge-snapshot.sh chunks at the declaration keyword and has three decoupled roles -- a `def`/`theorem`/`lemma`/named-`instance` both contributes its name to the cross-validated identifier set (which MUST equal the `- **Goals**:` set) AND gets its body force-rewritten to `:= sorry`, which would break every pinned theorem referencing it. An `abbrev` keeps its real body verbatim and contributes no name, so carrier definitions can sit in the block without appearing in Goals. Two companion facts: a per-declaration `open X in` prefix is stripped by the extractor (open at the top of the block instead, and note in the plan that the real module keeps the `open ... in` form); and `lean-challenge-snapshot.sh <task> <root> --dry-run --compile` compile-checks the assembled module against the project's own toolchain, so every pinned signature can be proven well-formed at PLAN time rather than discovered wrong mid-implementation.
